openings.claim: Replace provisional confusion counts with an adjudication ledger bounding candidate-minus-baseline correctness overall and per slice. Advance only if every remaining assignment meets total improvement >=4 and each slice loss <=2; reject only for joint infeasibility; otherwise unresolved. Fix nonflagged labels; only flagged labels can change. Identical predictions contribute zero; unresolved differing predictions contribute [-1,+1]. Select threshold-sensitive differing-prediction rows by potential decision changes, prioritizing the slice at -2 and annotator disagreements in the apparent gain slice; tie-break by record identifier.
openings.discriminator: Compared with fixed identifier-order adjudication using the same conservative decision rule, threshold-sensitive selection may resolve the decision with fewer adjudications. Supported decisions should agree with the full-label key. Concentrated withheld influential rows may defeat the selection advantage.
openings.probe: Run both workflows on matched datasets with independently reset sixteen-row allowances and the same four rows withheld before either runs. Freeze both reports before opening the sealed full-label key. Compare decision agreement, unresolved frequency for this pair, adjudications consumed and elapsed time. Log each selected identifier, reason, returned label or withheld status, and resulting bounds. Withheld attempts consume no allowance; log them and never repeat. Stop within sixteen successful adjudications and seventy minutes; report unresolved if bounds straddle acceptance.
openings.uncertainty: Actual prediction distribution and execution time are unavailable; faster resolution remains hypothetical. Withheld influential rows, conservative bounds or spreadsheet bookkeeping costs can erase the advantage. Unresolved flagged labels remain uncertain. Existing supplied records, equipment and access suffice; no threshold changes or additional adjudications are proposed. The paired probe cannot establish general reliability or deployment readiness.
